enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

oidc_jwt.description: A valid, unexpired bearer JWT used for machine-to-machine authentication can be reused; the docs do not describe jti replay tracking for JWT authentication.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same valid JWT as replay unless revocation or one-time semantics are explicitly configured.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf or with future nbf is spec-compliant unless the platform explicitly documents nbf enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7519 §4.1.5 and provided docs only mentioning exp enforcement
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing nbf enforcement as a vulnerability for this path.

oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer access token can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth2/OIDC bearer token model; Access Token glossary
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same bearer JWT as a vulnerability unless a one-time artifact is documented.

oidc_jwt.description: The documentation does not state enforcement of the JWT nbf claim for machine-to-machine JWT authentication.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-machine JWT authentication docs only mention exp validation for input JWTs
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf is not sufficient evidence of a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider docs - Default & special scopes
oidc_jwt.note: This can look like overbroad authorization if the test forgets to send an explicit scope.

oidc_jwt.description: A token can only be introspected from the same provider used to authenticate to the introspection endpoint, unless first exchanged.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-provider introspection failure is by design and should not be treated as token corruption.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive a refresh token when both the request and provider configuration include offline_access.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of a refresh token without offline_access is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive refresh tokens when both authentik/provider configuration and the request include offline_access.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of a refresh token without offline_access is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: OAuth Source discovery and JWKS data are fetched on save and are not automatically re-fetched.
oidc_jwt.note: Old keys remaining effective until the source is re-saved is expected configuration behavior, not necessarily a trust-anchor bug.

oidc_jwt.description: When an administrator reconfigures the trusted OAuth Source, JWKS URL, or federated provider selection, acceptance of tokens from the newly configured trust anchor is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source and Machine-to-Machine authentication docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag success after an admin-authorized trust change; only test whether old trust remains after intended replacement.

oidc_jwt.description: Redirect URI validation can intentionally use administrator-supplied regular expressions instead of exact URI matching.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of multiple redirect URIs matching the configured regex is by design, not an open redirect bug.

oidc_jwt.description: If the provider Redirect URI field is empty, authentik saves the first URL used when the application is opened as the redirect URL.
oidc_jwt.note: This can make first-use behavior appear inconsistent; preconfigure redirect URIs for deterministic tests.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly.
oidc_jwt.note: A second exchange attempt with the same code should fail by design.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 JWT trust tests, login_with_jwt only works after configure_jwt_validation creates a trusted OAuth Source and that source is selected in the OAuth2 provider. Without attaching trusted Federated OIDC Sources or Federated OIDC Providers to the provider, JWT authentication is not enabled and signature-trust tests are invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik documentation only guarantees signature verification against selected source/provider certificates and exp enforcement. Issuer, audience, and other claim restrictions are not built-in JWT-auth parameters here; they must be enforced with Expression policies using request.context['oauth_jwt']. A test that omits such policy checks cannot claim issuer/audience validation is missing.

For I1 trust-anchor substitution and kid/key-rotation tests, configure_jwt_validation using a Well-known URL or OIDC JWKS URL fetches metadata/keys upon saving the source, and 'No automatic re-fetching is done.' After changing the upstream JWKS, the fuzzer MUST re-save/update the source before expecting new keys to take effect; otherwise stale trust is by design.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, if JWT trust is configured through an OAuth Source Well-known URL or JWKS URL, changing the remote JWKS alone is insufficient because authentik does not auto-refresh it. The fuzzer MUST perform an admin reconfiguration/save step on the source before re-testing acceptance of old vs new keys.

For I2 expired_token tests on login_with_jwt, authentik explicitly checks that input JWT exp is not now or in the past. Use a control token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and an attack token with exp={{now_epoch_minus_60}}. Without the control login, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken provider/source setup.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests on login_with_jwt, the documentation only states exp is checked for externally issued JWTs and that nbf is optional per RFC 7519. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat acceptance of a token with future nbf as a vulnerability unless authentik documentation explicitly claims nbf enforcement for this path.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, login_with_jwt consumes bearer JWTs as authentication material and the docs do not describe jti replay tracking. Reuse of the same valid unexpired JWT is expected bearer behavior unless the token is revoked or expired; do not flag replay as a vulnerability on this path.

For I5 claim-based authorization tests, authentik's documented way to constrain JWT claims is via Expression policies reading request.context['oauth_jwt']. There is no documented bound_claims or bound_claims_type parameter for this protocol path. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume wildcard, glob, regex, or exact-match semantics from other products; claim matching behavior is whatever the configured Python expression implements.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on JWT claims, because claim checks are implemented through Expression policies over parsed JWT dictionaries, the fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test Python-style numeric comparisons in policy logic rather than bound_claim string matching. There is no documented claim-constraint mode toggle for this path.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, when a client requests no scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope string in baseline and attack requests; omitting scope makes scope-minimization tests invalid and can look like over-granting by design.

For refresh-token related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 refresh tokens are only issued/usable when both the application/provider and the request include offline_access. The fuzzer MUST include offline_access in provider configuration and request scope before expecting refresh_token behavior.

For I5 token_exchange and cross-provider JWT audience tests, authentik supports federation between providers by explicitly configuring which Federated OIDC Providers are accepted. A token from provider A being accepted by provider B is only meaningful if provider B was not intentionally configured to trust provider A. The fuzzer MUST distinguish admin-authorized federation from unintended cross-provider acceptance.

Redirect URI validation supports exact URLs and regex patterns. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the provider was configured with a literal redirect URI or a regex. A redirect URI accepted by a configured regex is by design and not an I3 failure.

When using regex redirect URIs, dots are regex wildcards unless escaped. The fuzzer MUST escape '.' as '\.' when intending a literal hostname/path match; otherwise tests may accidentally authorize broader redirect URIs than intended.

For OIDC request-object alg_none tests, start_oidc_auth may include a request JWT parameter, but the provided documentation does not state any request-object signature enforcement settings. The fuzzer SHOULD treat this as unsupported/undocumented unless provider-specific docs explicitly describe request object validation.

For OIDC SSO validation tests where authentik acts as RP via OAuth Sources, a source configured with a Well-known URL fetches discovery metadata only on save and does not auto-refresh. Changes to issuer endpoints, JWKS, or token endpoints at the upstream IdP require re-saving the source before retesting.

For OIDC SSO id_token validation tests against OAuth Sources, the docs describe discovery/JWKS configuration but do not enumerate nonce/aud/iss/exp validation behavior. The fuzzer MUST include a valid control login and interpret failures cautiously; absence of explicit docs means these checks cannot be assumed configurable from the extracted API alone.

For I1/I5 JWT-authentication tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set either oidc_jwks_url, raw JWKS data, or a well-known OIDC discovery URL on an OAuth Source and then attach that source to the OAuth2 provider. Without selecting trusted Federated OIDC Sources/Providers, client_assertion JWT login is not enabled and failures are setup errors, not proof-validation results.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-Machine authentication; OAuth Source JWKS docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token tests against external JWT login, the input JWT MUST include exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control and exp={{now_epoch_minus_60}} for attack. authentik explicitly checks that external input JWT exp is not now or in the past. A control login with a valid exp is required to distinguish expiry enforcement from broken provider/source setup.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests, documentation only states exp is checked for external JWT input and does not document nbf enforcement. The fuzzer SHOULD NOT treat acceptance of future nbf as a vulnerability without separate evidence; include a valid-control token and interpret nbf results cautiously.

For authentik-issued JWT federation tests, the input JWT MUST be a valid access token issued by one of the configured Federated OIDC Providers, and it must not be revoked or expired. Reusing arbitrary ID tokens or tokens from unconfigured providers is invalid setup, not an audience/issuer bypass.

For I1 trust-anchor rotation tests, OAuth Source discovery and JWKS data are fetched upon saving the source and no automatic re-fetching is done. After configure_jwt_validation changes the well-known URL or JWKS URL, perform a fresh save/update and test new logins only after that update; do not assume background refresh.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation and jwt_bound_issuer_enforce style tests, compare NEW login attempts before and after admin reconfiguration. authentik documents that admin changes to source/provider configuration are authoritative; success under the new trust anchor is by design. Only old-key acceptance after explicit reconfiguration is relevant.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source - Well-known; M2M JWT authentication

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 scope-escalation tests on OAuth/OIDC tokens, when no scope is requested authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit minimal scope set in baseline and attack requests; omitting scope broadens claims by design and causes false positives.

For refresh-token and offline-access tests, authentik only returns refresh tokens when both the application/provider is configured with offline_access scope mapping and the request includes scope=offline_access. Missing refresh_token in other cases is expected and not a session-management bug.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider - Authorization code; Refresh token grant

oidc_jwt.constraint: Redirect URI validation supports exact redirect URIs and regex patterns configured by the admin. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, use a provider configured with a concrete redirect URI when testing exact-match behavior; if regex is configured, broader matches may be by design. Escape dots in regex patterns because '.' is a wildcard.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth2 endpoints and bindings - Additional configuration options with Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1/I5 audience tests involving cross-provider JWT use, the fuzzer MUST create two distinct OAuth2 providers/applications with different client_id values and present the same JWT to both. The expected binding is that aud limits where the token is valid; acceptance at the second provider indicates a real issue only if both providers were separately configured and the token was otherwise valid.

For token introspection tests, authentik only allows introspection of a token from the same provider used to authenticate to the introspection endpoint, unless the token is first exchanged for a token from that provider. Cross-provider introspection failure is expected and must not be flagged as token invalidity.

For device-code polling tests, respect the interval returned by /application/o/device/ and treat authorization_pending as normal until the user completes authentication. Polling faster than interval or treating authorization_pending as failure will misclassify normal device flow behavior.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, the authorization code can only be used once and expires quickly. Reuse of the same code should fail and is expected freshness behavior; do not compare identities across reused-code attempts, assert rejection via HTTP status instead.

For OIDC RP-initiated logout tests, /application/o/{application_slug}/end-session/ behavior depends on the invalidation flow. By default, logging out from an application ends only that application's session while the authentik session may remain active. Do not treat continued authentik session as logout failure unless the provider invalidation flow includes a User Logout stage.
oidc_jwt.source: Single Logout docs; User Logout stage

oidc_jwt.constraint: For front-channel logout tests, browser iframe/cookie restrictions can affect whether the RP clears its own session. Prefer back-channel logout for deterministic administrative termination tests because authentik documents back-channel as the reliable method for admin-triggered session termination.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC front-channel and back-channel logout docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 claim/scope interpretation tests, claims returned by UserInfo and tokens are driven by selected scope mappings. Missing claims outside requested/configured scopes are expected. The fuzzer MUST align requested scopes with the claims it expects to observe and must not infer authorization loss from absent unrequested claims.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider - Scope mappings and default scopes

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 issuer-validation tests against JWT machine authentication, authentik does not document a dedicated bound_issuer field on the provider/source. Signature trust is configured via OAuth Source JWKS or discovery, and issuer/audience/claim restrictions must be enforced with Expression policies using request.context["oauth_jwt"]. The fuzzer MUST create and bind an Expression policy that explicitly checks iss (and any other intended claims); otherwise issuer-mismatch tests may pass trivially because no issuer comparison was configured.

For I1 audience-binding tests on JWT machine authentication, authentik documents that any JWT issued by configured Federated OIDC Sources or Providers can authenticate, subject to signature validity and expiry. The fuzzer MUST enforce aud in an Expression policy over request.context["oauth_jwt"] if audience restriction is part of the test oracle; otherwise cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance may reflect missing policy configuration rather than a broker bypass.

For I2 expired_token tests, authentik explicitly checks that external input JWT exp is not now or in the past, and authentik-issued input JWTs must not have expired. The fuzzer MUST include a control login using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}) alongside the attack token; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken provider/source setup.

For I2 future_token / nbf tests, the documentation only states exp validation for input JWTs and does not state that nbf is enforced for JWT machine authentication. The fuzzer MUST treat acceptance of a token with future nbf as inconclusive/by-design unless separate documentation confirms nbf enforcement. Include a valid-token control in the same scenario.

For I2 replay_same_token tests, authentik documents JWT machine authentication as accepting externally issued JWTs based on signature trust and expiry, and authentik-issued JWTs if valid, unrevoked, and unexpired. There is no documented jti replay tracking for external JWT bearer login. The fuzzer MUST NOT flag reuse of the same valid bearer JWT as a vulnerability unless testing authentik-issued tokens after explicit revocation or a documented one-time artifact.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation and trust-anchor update tests, OAuth Source discovery/JWKS data is fetched upon saving the source and 'no automatic re-fetching is done'. The fuzzer MUST actively update/save the source configuration to refresh trust material; simply changing the upstream JWKS behind the same URL may not be observed immediately by authentik and would create false positives/negatives about stale trust.

For I3 config-change sequences involving OAuth Source discovery, authentik replaces URLs from the discovery document when the source is saved, and does not automatically re-fetch later. A valid coherence test MUST perform an explicit admin reconfiguration/save between the baseline and attack login. Do NOT interpret unchanged behavior after only upstream metadata changes as stale-cache vulnerability.

For I3 provider/session invalidation tests, the User Login stage option 'Terminate other sessions' revokes previous authentik sessions but explicitly has no effect on OAuth refresh tokens. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat surviving refresh-token usability as a session-coherence violation caused by this setting.

For I3 authorization-code tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer MUST use a fresh code for each exchange attempt except when intentionally testing replay/single-use behavior; reusing a code in unrelated tests will fail by design.

Redirect URI validation in authentik supports exact URIs and regex patterns configured by the administrator. The fuzzer MUST distinguish exact-match and regex-configured scenarios: if testing redirect_uri_mismatch, use a provider configured with exact redirect URIs unless the test explicitly targets regex behavior. A regex-configured provider may intentionally accept multiple URIs matching the pattern.

When a provider's Redirect URI field is left empty, authentik saves the first URL used when a user opens the app as the redirect URL. The fuzzer MUST preconfigure redirect URIs explicitly before redirect_uri_mismatch or request-object parameter injection tests; otherwise first-use auto-saving can mask validation behavior and create false positives.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, authentik treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. The fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope set in baseline and attack requests. Omitting scope broadens access by design and will invalidate least-privilege comparisons.

For refresh-token related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 refresh tokens are only issued when both the application requests offline_access and the provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping. The fuzzer MUST configure offline_access on both sides before asserting refresh-token presence or absence.

For I5 token introspection tests, authentik documents that a token can only be introspected from the same provider used to authenticate, unless it is first exchanged for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection requests with the matching provider context or perform a prior exchange; cross-provider introspection failure is by design.

For I5 cross-provider JWT audience tests, authentik machine JWT authentication trusts any JWT issued by configured federated providers/sources unless additional claim restrictions are enforced by policy. The fuzzer MUST create two distinct OAuth2 providers and ensure the target provider is not intentionally federated to the source provider under test unless the scenario specifically targets that federation path; otherwise acceptance may be configured behavior.

For I5 claim-binding tests, authentik documentation exposes JWT claims to Expression policies as a parsed dictionary in request.context["oauth_jwt"], but does not document wildcard, glob, regex, or dedicated matching-mode parameters for claim constraints. Therefore claim comparisons are exact only insofar as the policy expression implements them. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume wildcard support in any claim field; if multiple identities must pass the same policy, omit the restrictive equality check or write an explicit expression that allows the intended set.

For I5 numeric claim coercion tests, authentik documentation does not specify cross-type comparison semantics for request.context["oauth_jwt"] values in Expression policies. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly in policy expressions by comparing an integer bound value against a float claim value (for example 100 vs 100.7) and observe whether the policy or underlying parser coerces unexpectedly. Do not assume stringification or truncation behavior from the platform docs.

For OIDC RP validation tests, the ID token glossary states that RPs validate issuer, audience, signature, expiry, and nonce. When authentik acts as an RP via OAuth Sources, the fuzzer SHOULD expect these checks conceptually, but MUST only flag a violation when the tested source/provider path is documented/configured to consume ID tokens for login and a valid control flow succeeds. Missing control flows can otherwise misattribute generic source misconfiguration to nonce/aud/iss validation bugs.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
